questions.q: What is a digital signature, in the class's own words?
options: A virtual fingerprint for documents, proving authenticity and integrity
A picture of your handwritten signature scanned into a computer
A type of cryptocurrency wallet
A password used to log into a website
questions.explain: A digital signature cryptographically proves a message was created by a specific person and hasn't been altered — the class's own analogy is a virtual fingerprint.

questions.q: What are the actual steps to creating a digital signature?
options: Hash the message, then encrypt that hash using your private key — the encrypted hash becomes the signature
Simply type your name at the bottom of the message
Send the message twice to prove it's really from you
Encrypt the message using the recipient's private key
questions.explain: You hash the message first, then encrypt that hash with your own private key — that encrypted hash is the actual digital signature.

questions.q: What does anyone need to verify that a digital signature is genuine?
options: The sender's public key
The sender's private key
Nothing — signatures can't actually be verified
A password shared in advance
questions.explain: Because the signature was created with the sender's private key, anyone holding the matching public key can verify it — without ever needing the private key itself.

questions.q: In the wax-stamp analogy, what does the unique stamp represent?
options: The digital signature, proving the letter came from a specific person and wasn't tampered with
The message content itself
The recipient's identity
A physical envelope
questions.explain: Just as a unique wax stamp shows a letter genuinely came from its sender and wasn't altered, a digital signature does the same thing online.

questions.q: What does "non-repudiation" mean, as one of the three things a digital signature proves?
options: The sender can't later deny that they signed the message
The message can be edited after signing with no consequence
Anyone can claim they sent the message
The signature expires after 24 hours
questions.explain: Non-repudiation means that once you've signed something with your private key, you can't credibly claim later that you didn't — a key property for binding blockchain transactions.
